P41.answer: The word is taken to begin with my Stage 1 pos 6 (ה/ח at A x~525-610, B x~410-520, C x~350-425). Its letters to the left are my Stage 1 pos 7 (A x~395-495) and the [...] zone. Re-examination for this question (reason: looking at whether the left upright of pos 7 is joined): in B the left upright (B x~297) stops a little short of the left end of the base (gap of ~20 px), and in C the left side is hidden by a bright streak. So the Stage 1 'ט' may be two signs: a box letter (right upright + short top + base) and a separate upright to its left. The ה itself: left leg not clearly joined to the top bar in A/B/C (ה probable, ח possible). A gap of ~40 px separates it from the stroke on its right (pos 5), but I cannot confirm a word space.
P41.evidence: A, B, C as cited; D too faint to judge the gap.

P41.answer: Neither definition fits cleanly. Base: flat and straight in A, B and C; it ends at the right upright with a square lower-right corner. No projection beyond the upright in B or C. In A there is at most a ~10 px overrun at the corner, which could be the shadow of the relief. Top: a short top stroke runs left from the head of the right upright, and its left end turns upward into a small tick. This is clear in B (an L-shaped stroke at B x~360-400, y~265-310) and C (C x~280-315), and in A it shows as a short stroke inside the top right (A x~455-470). No full-width top bar. Because there is no projection I lean slightly to כ, but the square corner is against כ's rounded form.
P41.evidence: B and C (X-rays) are decisive for the absence of projection; A shows the corner most sharply; D shows a box with a top stroke over its right half and a dark band that runs on to the right, but that runs into the next letter's area and is not reliable.

P41.answer: ו rather than י. It is a full-height upright (A x~395, y~225-350; B x~297, y~270-410) and reaches the base line, so it is not a short hanging י. No head or hook at its top in A or B. Caveat: it may instead be the left side of the preceding letter (giving the Stage 1 ט). In A it touches the base; in B it is separate.
P41.evidence: A, B; C obscured by bright streak; D shows a dark upright at about this place.

P41.answer: After the upright there is one possible further sign. A small loop or hook in the upper half of the line, at A x~305-335 (round bulge, y~215-280), corresponds to B x~210-235 (small open loop, y~260-300). In both it sits on a vertical crack that would swallow any stem. It could be the head of ז/ו/ר, or only a crack feature. Is there a ז: only possibly, at this hook. I cannot confirm a ז. Last visible letter: the upright ו (possible), or this hook if it is a letter. The word does not visibly run to the plate edge. Left of the crack (A x~60-290) A shows only vertical shadows. D shows a smooth, apparently uninscribed surface (D x~80-240). In B and C, left of the crack, there are only streaks and fine cracks. So the line seems to end at or just after the crack, which could hide about one letter.
P41.evidence: A, B and D agree that no strokes are visible left of the crack. C shows a bright streak and a black crack gap there.

P56.answer: I cannot locate a pair like ככ. Near the left end the readable marks, from the right, are as follows. A x~700-790: faint slanting strokes. A x~600-700: two strong vertical creases. A x~505-600: rough surface with a small hooked stroke (x~567-593). A x~330-505: a flaked-off chip. Then the signs described in (a) and (b). None of these is a clear box letter.
P56.evidence: A only; B has no legible strokes in this region.

P56.answer: Signs other than vertical strokes: (1) at A x~185-290, two heavy diagonals converging downward (V shape, meeting at about y~255). This could be a letter (my Stage 1 ע) or a non-stroke sign. (2) A small triangular outline at A x~150-190 (y~213-243). Its lines are thin and continuous with the horizontal crack, so it is probably a crack loop, not a sign. Nothing hook-shaped or curled is certain.
P56.evidence: A (enhanced); B shows only a crack and a dark loss here.

P56.answer: Count of vertical unit strokes: cannot tell. At most two thin faint verticals at A x~305-317 and ~330-337 (y~150-240). They may be strokes or fine cracks. The two strong verticals at A x~607-633 and ~660-690 are creases running through every line (B shows a white crease there), so they are not unit strokes. No grouping can be seen.
P56.evidence: A; B shows no strokes. A cleaner X-ray of the left third, or a raking-light photo of the original, would be needed.

P56.answer: Yes, there is much damage. (1) A flaked-off chip at A x~330-505 (y~190-330), with no surface left. B shows a dark loss at B x~265-440. Room for several strokes or 1-2 letters. (2) Vertical creases at A x~600-700. (3) A horizontal crack at about y~240-250 runs across A x~100-500 through the middle of the line and could hide short strokes. (4) A rough, pitted surface at A x~500-600. (5) The left margin (A x~90-150) is near the plate edge.
P56.evidence: A and B both show the chip/loss and cracks.

P63.answer: Candidate pair: my Stage 1 pos 2 (A x~1050-1215, ב/כ, base projects right) and pos 4 (A x~800-905, box letter with a short top over its right half, base, right upright). Between them is pos 3, a dark upright at A x~1000-1035 that coincides with a crack. If pos 3 is only the crack, then pos 2 and pos 4 form a pair of box letters. They are not identical: pos 2 has a projecting base, and in pos 4 the projection is unclear.
P63.evidence: A; B has a white crease over pos 3-4 and shows only base lines (B x~990-1130 and ~790-860).

P63.answer: Signs to the left of the pair, right to left. (1) A x~640-775: a U-shaped curled sign. It has a long left upright (partly coinciding with a through-crack, B x~590-660), a flat base, and a right arm whose top curls inward to the left. This is my Stage 1 'ט'. Probable as a shape. (2) A x~510-600: a rounded arch or inverted V. In B (x~440-540) it is a clear ∩ outline with an inner diagonal; in D a raised dome. Possible. (3) A x~385-490: a rounded arch with a heavy right leg. B (x~285-430) shows ∩ with a doubled stroke (two lines in a V) at the right leg, and A shows a doubled stroke at its left (x~340 and ~372). This sign may be doubled: possible. So there are three large curved/hook-like signs (1 curled U + 2 arches), and the leftmost may be doubled. (4) Thin vertical strokes at A x~257, ~313 and ~340 are clear, ~290 is faint, and ~372 may instead be the arch's left leg. That gives 3 certain-looking + 2 doubtful, so a count of 3-5. Best estimate 4 (possible). They form one run spaced ~25-30 px apart, with no clear gap dividing them into groups. B shows only one of them (B x~200-210 = A ~257). D shows uprights near D x~275-290. (5) A x~170-215: a dark diagonal hook-like mark, either a sign or a crack (illegible).
P63.evidence: A for the strokes (a column darkness profile shows minima at x~255, 312, 340, 370-385), B for the arch outlines, D for the domes. My Stage 1 letter readings ט ח ח for signs 1-3 are equally compatible with numeral signs. I do not decide between letters and numerals.

P63.answer: Yes. (1) A through-crack runs along the left upright of sign 1 (A x~650-665 / B x~590-660) and could hide a stroke. (2) A crack along pos 3. (3) B has white creases at B x~760-900, so it is blind over pos 3-4. (4) The surface at A x~130-250 is rough and the tops of the strokes merge with the line above, so a short stroke at the far left could be lost.

P92.answer: I cannot locate a word beginning כ-פ. The nearest candidates are the two curled letters (Stage 1 pos 4 at A x~737-853 and pos 5 at A x~545-720). In both, the right upright's top turns left and curls down inside. With a closed left upright that is ט. The same top would be פ if the left upright were separate. In B (x~637) the left upright of pos 4 looks like a separate vertical with its own small head to the left, so 'פ + upright' is possible for pos 4. But there is no כ immediately to its right: pos 3 is a long single upright. So the כ-פ pair is not found.
P92.evidence: A and B (enhanced). The two curled letters are clear in both images; their identity (ט vs פ) depends on the left upright.

P92.answer: Since the word was not found, I give the letters that follow (to the left of) the curled pair: pos 6, a short upright at A x~510-535 (y~160-245), with possibly a head or step at x~540-580 — י/ו/ר, possible. Pos 7, a long straight stroke at A x~450-495 descending below the base line — ן, possible (or ו, or part of the next letter). Pos 8, at A x~360-445, an upright ending in a thick tail down-left — ע, possible (alternatives צ, נ). Pos 9 and 10 are illegible, crowded against the line above. No word space is visible to separate words.
P92.evidence: A; B confirms the long diagonal (B x~330-365) and a top bar with an upright (B x~383-485), not the identities.

P92.answer: The short upright + long descending stroke (pos 6-7) could be ין: possible. No ם (closed box) is seen there. A ר is possible only if pos 6 has a head, which is uncertain. I cannot say which letter ends the word, because no word boundary is visible.
Cannot tell. No word boundaries are visible on the left part of the line.

No numeral signs are identified on the target line. There are no groups of short unit strokes and no hook signs separate from letters. The left third (A x<450) is crowded and creased, and could hide small strokes.
